package_inventory.notes: lakefile.toml declares only mathlib, so there is no non-Mathlib package inventory to record for the opening Chapter 1 batch.

sources.citation: Andrew V. Sutherland, 18.785 Number Theory I, Lecture #1: Absolute values and discrete valuations (MIT, Fall 2021).
sources.reason: This is the closest statement-level match to the opening-batch blobs: it contains the introduction, the absolute-value definitions, the nonarchimedean criterion, the p-adic definition, Ostrowski's theorem, and the product formula in essentially the same form as the transcribed lecture.
formalization_leads: Use this as the canonical prose reference when Stage 3 formalization needs the exact wording or surrounding context of the opening batch.
It confirms that Lemma 1.4, Theorem 1.8, and Theorem 1.9 are intentionally deferred to Problem Set 1 rather than proved in the lecture notes.

sources.citation: Andrew V. Sutherland, 18.785 Number Theory I, Problem Set #1 (MIT, Fall 2021).
sources.reason: This source contains the exact proof obligations omitted from the lecture: the nonarchimedean characterization in Lemma 1.4, Ostrowski's theorem on Q, and the product formula on Q.
formalization_leads: Treat it as the primary natural-language proof source for the current Mathlib gaps around Lemma 1.4 and the product formula on Q.
Its parallel F_q(t) exercises are useful for keeping the lecture's number-field and function-field analogies aligned in later formalization.

sources.citation: Andrew V. Sutherland, 18.785 Number Theory I, Lecture #9: Local fields and Hensel's lemmas (MIT, Fall 2021).
sources.reason: The introduction frames local fields as completions of global fields, and these later notes supply that completion-to-local-field background in the same course vocabulary.
formalization_leads: Use it when later blobs need the precise local-field facts alluded to in the introduction's discussion of R and Q_p.
It gives the natural follow-on source for completion and valuation-ring language that reappears after the opening batch.

sources.citation: Andrew V. Sutherland, 18.785 Number Theory I, Lecture #13: Global fields and the product formula (MIT, Fall 2021).
sources.reason: These notes revisit the same place/completion language from the opening lecture and then package the product formula in the broader global-field setting, which is useful once the local Q result is formalized.
formalization_leads: Use it to normalize terminology around places, completions, and finite versus infinite places before writing later reference blobs.
It provides the clearest course-internal bridge from the opening-batch Q statements to the later global-field product-formula formalization.

sources.reason: The lecture explicitly cites Serre as a reference for much of Section 1.2, so this is the natural book-level source for the absolute-value background, p-adic constructions, and surrounding local-field context.
formalization_leads: Use it when later stages need a durable book reference rather than course-specific notes for the opening-batch absolute-value material.
It is the best source in the lecture bibliography for filling in background that the lecture states but does not prove.
